panels.title: What this dashboard cannot tell you

options.content:
**Consumer lag, feed staleness and module liveness are NOT here.** They are not in InfluxDB — they live on each module's health endpoint (`127.0.0.1:9800+offset/health`), because they describe a *process*, not an event, and archiving them would mean the archiver reporting on its own health.

Point a Grafana **Infinity** or JSON datasource at those endpoints, or scrape them with whatever already watches your processes. A panel here querying Influx for them would be permanently empty, which is worse than an honest gap — an empty panel reads as *"nothing is wrong"*.

**P&L vs. backtest expectation** is also absent: reconciliation output is written to `state/sessions/`, not to Influx. Run `python -m src.briefing evening`.

panels.title: Order flow — signals, approvals, fills
panels.description: The three counts should track each other. Signals far above approvals means the risk engine is refusing most of them, which is information: a day where twenty signals became three trades looks identical in P&L to a day with three signals, and diverges from the backtest for a completely different reason.

targets.query:
signals = from(bucket: v.bucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "trade_signals" and r._field == "ref_price")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: count, createEmpty: true)
  |> set(key: "_field", value: "signals")

approved = from(bucket: v.bucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "approved_orders" and r._field == "quantity")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: count, createEmpty: true)
  |> set(key: "_field", value: "approved")

fills = from(bucket: v.bucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "filled_orders" and r._field == "filled_quantity")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: count, createEmpty: true)
  |> set(key: "_field", value: "fills")

union(tables: [signals, approved, fills])

panels.title: Order outcomes
panels.description: One rejection is routine. A run of them is systemic — a wrong symbol, an expired session, a product code the account cannot use — and the strategy keeps signalling into it.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.bucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "filled_orders")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "status")
  |> group(columns: ["_value"])
  |> count()

panels.title: Dead-lettered messages
panels.description: Work the system gave up on. Any non-zero value needs a human: on approved_orders it means a trade was never placed. Should be zero.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.bucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "dead_letter")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "error")
  |> count()

panels.title: Tick throughput
panels.description: The archive's view of the feed. A drop to zero during market hours means the feed died — but confirm against the module's health endpoint before concluding it, because a flat line here could equally be the archiver falling behind.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.bucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "market_ticks")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "ltp")
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: count, createEmpty: true)

panels.title: Bars built
panels.description: The historical dataset accumulating (D5 mitigation 2). This is the slowest-maturing asset in the project.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.bucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "market_bars")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "close")
  |> count()

panels.title: Recent rejections and errors
panels.description: The reason text, not just the count. During an incident a rejection reason that names the wrong subsystem sends whoever is on the keyboard down the wrong path.

targets.query:
from(bucket: v.bucket)
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "filled_orders" or r._measurement == "dead_letter")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "error" or r._field == "reason")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._value != "")
  |> sort(columns: ["_time"], desc: true)
  |> limit(n: 50)
